gloss: to shake one's head (in refusal or disagreement)

definitions.gloss: to shake one's head; to say no; to refuse
definitions.explanation: The physical gesture of shaking one's head side to side to express disagreement, refusal, or denial. Also used figuratively for declining or rejecting something.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{首|くび}を{横|よこ}に{振|ふ}った。
{頼|たの}んだが、{首|くび}を{横|よこ}に{振|ふ}られた。
examples.english: I asked, but was met with a shake of the head.

examples.japanese: {何度|なんど}{説得|せっとく}しても、{彼|かれ}は{首|くび}を{横|よこ}に{振|ふ}るばかりだった。
examples.english: No matter how many times I tried to persuade him, he just kept shaking his head.

notes:
Literally 'to swing one's neck sideways.' In Japanese, {首|くび} (neck) is used where English uses 'head' for the shaking gesture.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {首|くび}を{横|よこ}に{振|ふ}る — to shake one's head (no, refusal)
- {首|くび}を{縦|たて}に{振|ふ}る — to nod (yes, agreement)

The pair {横|よこ} (horizontal) vs. {縦|たて} (vertical) makes the distinction explicit.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {首|くび}を{横|よこ}に{振|ふ}る — plain statement
- {首|くび}を{横|よこ}に{振|ふ}られる — passive: to be refused (someone shook their head at me)
- {首|くび}を{横|よこ}に{振|ふ}るばかり — to do nothing but shake one's head

RELATED WORDS:
- {首|くび}を{縦|たて}に{振|ふ}る — to nod; to agree
- うなずく — to nod (a single word for the same gesture)
- {首|くび}をかしげる — to tilt one's head (in doubt or puzzlement)
